title: IterLoop personal logsheet — quick probe
content:
Purpose: super-light personal tracker for iterative latency/cost probes while I tinker with prefix caching + quantization combos. Not a canonical sheet — scratchpad style.

Context:
- Running small controlled probes on a reserved dev node (g4dn-like). Trying to capture p50/p95/p99 + tokens/sec + approximate cost per 1k tokens.
- Short IDs are local to this sheet (E-xxx).
- Use this when doing quick compare runs before filing a formal perf PR.

Quick legend:
- model: model variant (float16 / int4/ int8-ggml)
- quant: quantization method shorthand (Q4_0, Q4_1, PTQ8, INT8)
- batch: batch size used by the client
- seq: max sequence length used in run (prompt + gen)
- p99/p95/p50: latency percentiles (ms)
- tps: tokens per second observed (tokens/sec)
- cost1k: rough $ cost per 1k tokens (inference only, naive GPU-cost prorate)

Table (most recent at top):
| id      | date       | model        | quant  | batch | seq | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | tps  | cost1k($) | notes / anomalies | status |
|---------|------------|--------------|--------|-------|-----|---------:|--------:|--------:|-----:|----------:|-------------------|--------|
| E-2026-03A | 2026-03-09 | lw-13b-v2    | Q4_1   | 8     | 1024|    34   |   120   |   210   |  480 | 0.012     | weird tail at >900 tokens, saw batch queuing spike at t=00:32 | draft  |
| E-2026-03B | 2026-03-09 | lw-13b-v2    | PTQ8   | 8     | 1024|    40   |   150   |   260   |  420 | 0.009     | slightly slower but lower cost; quantizing changed sample variance | draft  |
| E-2026-02Z | 2026-02-27 | rw-7b-lite   | INT8   | 16    | 512 |    22   |    80   |   110   |  900 | 0.006     | baseline for 7b experiments, clean tail | final  |
| E-2026-01X | 2026-01-18 | lw-13b-v2    | float16| 4     | 1024|    28   |   100   |   180   |  310 | 0.020     | small batch -> lower throughput but p50 good | archived|

Notes to self (actionable):
- Follow up: reproduce E-2026-03A tail with tracing flags on (env RUN_TRACING=1) — add stack traces for batching events. Linked ticket JIRA-ENG-4821.
- Try dynamic batching tweak: reduce max_batch_wait_ms from 10 -> 6 and rerun E-2026-03A to see tail impact.
- Evaluate cache warmup: run 50 short prefix-only probes to measure warm cache latency drop; compare p99 before/after.
- For cost numbers, standardize formula: (gpu_hour_rate / tokens_processed) * 1000 — need to confirm per-region rates with infra; current numbers are approximate.
- If PTQ8 continues to lower cost without unacceptable p99 increase, propose a canary rollout for non-critical routes (product-hosted-api).

Loose checklist (stop-gap before formal doc):
- [ ] Reproduce heavy-tail with batch_wait tweak
- [ ] Add perf trace export to S3 (small artifact)
- [ ] Tag reproducible run with Git SHA and PR link (see runtime PR 1324)
- [ ] Summarize into short Confluence perf note and attach sample traces

Observations / hypotheses (brain dump):
- Hypothesis A: tail correlated with occasional KV cache eviction + concurrent small prefix loads; batching scheduler sometimes groups late micro-requests leading to higher p99.
- Hypothesis B: PTQ8 shows lower cost but higher p99 variability — maybe kernel selection is less predictable under PTQ code paths.

Quick replication commands (local scratch):
- run_probe.sh --model lw-13b-v2 --quant Q4_1 --batch 8 --seq 1024 --runs 200 --out /tmp/E-2026-03A.json
- collect_traces.sh /tmp/E-2026-03A.json --upload s3://redwood-dev-perf/talia/

Random notes to self:
- Ask Maya about a small utility to convert these rows into CSV quickly for perf dashboard ingestion.
- Save best-run snapshot IDs in a tiny folder: /redwood/dev/runs/talia/ (manual for now).

End of sheet — ephemeral. If anything looks worth formalizing, move to shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/perf-notes/ with a proper template.
